original_question: Is there an analogue of the Nymann-Saenz Lemma for endpoints of interval components of an achievable Cantorval? More concretely, if E(x_n) is a Cantorval and a and b are left endpoints of two distinct interval components of E, must there exist epsilon > 0 such that E intersect [a - epsilon, a] is a translate of E intersect [b - epsilon, b]?
target_in_paper: The draft most likely targets an open problem in the paper’s Cantorval/open-problems discussion asking whether left endpoints of distinct interval components of an achievable Cantorval have the same local left-hand structure up to translation. I could verify from the arXiv record that arXiv:2512.17285 is a survey of current results and open problems, but I could not recover the exact open-problem number or page from the accessible browser copy. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content very well: it uses the achievement-set notation E(x_n), assumes the relevant topological type is a Cantorval, focuses on left endpoints of distinct interval components, and asks for a local translation-invariance statement of the form E ∩ [a-ε,a] versus E ∩ [b-ε,b]. That is already very close to a stand-alone open problem in the Cantorval literature. The emphasis on left endpoints is also paper-faithful to nearby work, where left edges of interval components are treated as the distinguished exceptional set. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00025-022-01777-3))
missing_details: State explicitly what E(x_n) means: E(x_n) = {\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n x_n : \varepsilon_n \in {0,1}}.
Specify the ambient class of sequences: typically a summable sequence of positive reals, and often nonincreasing in the achievement-set literature.
Define 'achievable Cantorval' explicitly as a Cantorval of the form E(x_n) for such a sequence.
Clarify that 'interval component' means a nondegenerate connected component of E(x_n), i.e. a closed interval contained in E(x_n).
Clarify that a and b are left endpoints of two distinct nontrivial interval components, not arbitrary boundary points.
Make the translation explicit: the natural shift is by b-a, so one should ask whether (E(x_n) ∩ [a-ε,a]) + (b-a) = E(x_n) ∩ [b-ε,b].
State whether ε is allowed to depend on the pair (a,b); the natural formulation is existential for each pair.
Remove the contextual phrase 'analogue of the Nymann-Saenz Lemma' from the final question unless that lemma is also restated, because otherwise the question is not fully stand-alone.
refined_question: Let (x_n) be a summable sequence of positive real numbers, and let E(x_n)=\{\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n x_n:\varepsilon_n\in\{0,1\}\}. Assume that E(x_n) is a Cantorval. If a and b are the left endpoints of two distinct nondegenerate interval components of E(x_n), must there exist ε>0 such that (E(x_n)∩[a-ε,a])+(b-a)=E(x_n)∩[b-ε,b]?
justification: This rewrite stays narrow and keeps the exact intent of your draft: it asks for local left-neighborhood rigidity at left endpoints of interval components of an achievable Cantorval, and nothing broader. I did not broaden it to general boundary points, arbitrary Cantorvals, or other classes of self-similar sets. The choice to single out left endpoints is consistent with nearby Cantorval literature, where left edges of interval components form the natural exceptional set, and with recent open-problem summaries emphasizing structural questions about Cantorvals and their boundaries. Because the accessible browser copy of arXiv:2512.17285 exposed only the abstract/metadata, I cannot honestly supply the exact internal label/page of the target problem from the paper itself; the formulation above is therefore a best paper-faithful reconstruction rather than a fully verified quotation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17285))
